tips: Build review requests into your handover routine: before you leave a job, ask every customer in person if they'd be willing to leave a review, and give them the link or write it down. Makes it immediate and personal.

Send a warm, brief text or WhatsApp within an hour of finishing, while the job is fresh in their mind. Keep it friendly and low-pressure: 'If you're happy with how it went, we'd love a review.' People respond better to genuine tone than sales talk.

In your job paperwork (invoice, quote, receipt), add a small line at the bottom with your Google review link and a simple 'If you're pleased with the work, we'd love your feedback.' No hard sell, just make it easy to find.

After a boiler service or repair, follow up with a text a week later: 'Just checking everything's running smoothly? If so, a review really helps us.' Timing it after they've had chance to see the work in action builds confidence.

Encourage your team to mention reviews in conversation during jobs. Keep it natural: 'We really rely on word-of-mouth and reviews from customers like you.' Family-run businesses can lean on that authenticity, people trust recommendations from real families.

If a customer compliments you during a job ('You've been really tidy,' 'That was a fair quote'), capture that moment: 'Thanks! If you'd be willing to mention that in a review, it'd mean the world to us.' Positive energy in the moment translates to action.

Create a simple system: add customer phone numbers to a spreadsheet and set calendar reminders to send follow-ups after 5–7 days if you haven't seen a review yet. Persistence is kind when it's brief and genuine.
